The 2025 Arizona's 7th congressional district special election was held on September 23, 2025, to fill Arizona's 7th congressional district for the remainder of the 119th United States Congress. The result was certified by the Arizona Secretary of State, Adrian Fontes, on October 14.[1]

This followed the July 15, 2025, primary election, the results of which were certified by Fontes 16 days later on July 31.

The seat became vacant following the death of incumbent Democrat Raúl Grijalva on March 13, 2025.

The election was won by former Pima County supervisor Adelita Grijalva, Raúl Grijalva's daughter.[2] The younger Grijalva won by 40%, a significant overperformance from Kamala Harris's 22% victory in the district in the 2024 presidential election.[3]

Background

[edit | edit source]

Incumbent Congressman Raúl Grijalva was diagnosed with lung cancer on April 2, 2024, and died in office on March 13, 2025, from complications from cancer treatments, at age 77.[4] Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs announced a special election to fill the vacancy would be held on September 23, 2025, with the primary set for July 15.[5] Due to the districts partisan lean, it is considered a safe Democratic.[6] Kamala Harris won the district by 22% in 2024, and the Democratic candidate was easily expected to win.[3]

Campaign and results

[edit | edit source]

Writing for The Arizona Republic in May, Laura Gersony believed that the leading candidates were former state Representative Daniel Hernández Jr., Grijalva's daughter Adelita Grijalva, and social media influencer Deja Foxx. Gersony noted that while Hernández held an initial lead in fundraising, which she attributed to his support for Israel, but that Grijalva would likely benefit from the campaign infrastructure built by her father.[56] Grijalva received the endorsement of both of Arizona's U.S. Senators, Mark Kelly and Ruben Gallego,[21] and a number of Democratic political organizations, including EMILYs List and Giffords.[34][33]
